utterances.text: I do not know if it was in June or in May. Our people went up to Visoko and that is when he joined them. He was called by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was this before or after the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the conflict in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: All right, was Sefkija Dzidic his commander, Sefkija Dzidic from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was the protector of the Territorial Defence. Whether he was at the school then or not, I do not know, I was not involved in these affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did your husband have weapons at home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not have anything. Afterwards, my son got some because they made some rifles from old rifles from Slimane.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Which son got these weapons from Slimane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My son Senus.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, they said that some barracks were burned and that some burned rifles were there and then our people made new rifles out of these old parts, but I do not know that anyone had any weapons then. Apart from this burned rifle from Slimane, I saw it when my son got it, the iron was burned down and I was laughing and I said, "you could not shoot a rabbit with this gun". I know that he was cleaning that rifle and trying to make something out of it, but it was all burned, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And your husband, when he was in the Territorial Defence, did he have weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, where was Senus on 16th April 1993 when all this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was asleep at his home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know how he survived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. On 18th October, everything was torched at his place. He was in Visoko then, everything was torched. He lived in the weekend cottage of Muhamed Spahic, underneath my house where refugees were staying. All of that was given to refugees and my son was staying there in the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Your son, was he in the Territorial Defence or the BH army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know about such matters, I am not very good at this. I think they were in the Territorial Defence. I do not know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And your other son Muamer, did he join the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina or the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence, he went as a volunteer to Visoko when he came back from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Your son came from the JNA, he was in Croatia. Did he take part in the war in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the war was on in Slovenia, he was there. When this was happening in Slovenia, we know that he was there and we could not reach him at all. We had no contact with him while he was in the army there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did he tell you where he was? Did he tell you that he was in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not tell me anything. Perhaps he told his brothers, but not me. I mean his brother, because they were very close, but I did not have such conversations with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, in the morning when the shooting began, did shooting come from the mosque? Was there some kind of Defence there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know a thing. I was in the house, people were on guard because we were in danger from October, so they were always on guard around our houses there and what happened there, I do not know, because the mosque was hit from afar. My husband was in the mosque when they went there to pray, the mosque was hit. A strong detonation was heard and that is when it all started.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who are the people who were on guard? These were your neighbours? Can you tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mirso Ahmic, I know him. I do not know the other names. Because my house is the last one and then I would only see the people who went by my house. I know Mirso who was on guard, but we women were not involved in such matters. We had trouble preparing the food, we were always afraid. We were always in danger from October onwards. For a period of time they would not even allow us to get out to the road. Ivo Papic would not let us get out to the road and he did not allow anyone to come and see us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So between October 1992 and April 1993, your relations with your Croat neighbours were not very good, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were very good before they divorced themselves from us. We used to call on each other before that, we used to visit, but they would not come afterwards, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When did the Croats divorce themselves from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How do you know that the mosque was hit, did you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told by someone, somebody called me on the phone, Hajji from the mosque, she called me, and she said that the mosque was hit. I had a telephone in the house, and she told me that the mosque was hit, but they were not shooting at our house yet, but I could not get out because my husband had locked me in and he went to the mosque and she said, "Hajrudin is here", so she told me that the mosque was hit. Celebija Ahmic was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, when you went to have a drink of water, you said that shooting was coming from all over. Could you tell us more precisely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The infantry bullets were flying all over. I know that -- I heard them above my head coming from all directions, but Zahir Ahmic was killed and Sacir from Karaula. He was a refugee, and his wife told me in the basement about Zahir and Sacir, Zilka her name was. I think they were shooting at me from Zahir's house as I was going to get a drink of water, because these houses were next door.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said bullets were coming from this side and that side, from everywhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from down there at the road, from everywhere, you could hear it all over. Who was not there cannot even imagine it, you cannot even describe it. The shooting was coming from the Papics’, you could hear the shooting but mostly they were shooting directly at the houses. That is what the people in the basement told me, but as far as I am concerned, I think that these soldiers from Zahir's house were shooting at me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you said that you went to take a drink of water and that bullets were coming from this side and that side, does that mean from all directions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the road and from the other side and the forest and the barn and the other side, so it was shooting all over from down there and up there, but then the barn and the forest and the house were some kind of protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you were going to your sister in Gornji Ahmici, can you tell us where the shooting was coming from then? From Grabovi to Donje Ahmici, from Gornji Ahmici to Donje Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could only see Gornji Ahmici when I came, that is where the sniper fire was coming from, but I could not see all the details. There was a lot of shooting but I was struggling to remain conscious, because I was greatly depressed, because two of my children were killed and I thought my husband was killed too. I did not mind being killed that much myself. I would go and then I would stop and then I would go and then I would stop again, sit down and that is how I reached my sister's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I put a direct question? From Gornji Ahmici, was there any shooting coming from Gornji Ahmici towards down there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, we have been talking for about three or four minutes about this firing. I think the witness has told you everything she knows about the direction from where the firings come. The witness has lost one child, she may have lost two. With firing going on all over, I do not think you need to ask about the strategic origins or whatever of the firing. She is not a military expert, she is more a victim than anything else, so please let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: All right, I have more or less concluded this line of questioning, although I just wanted to ask two things concerning the directions. The sniper was shooting from the Mejtef, can I clarify that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we came to Mejtef, our people were running from there because sniper fire was there and the Mejtef is high up and we were down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Under whose control was Mejtef?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Croats. Borik, Mejtef, Kratine, Bahra, Hrazne, all of that was under their control. We were surrounded all over.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that, "the people who were defending us were saying that the shooting came from the Kupreskics and they put furniture up to defend ourselves". Can you tell me, what did you see? What kind of furniture and who was defending you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around the house, these people who were with us were putting elements of furniture around the house. I saw some of this furniture there, because the house was in the forest and it was hit by shells and we tried to protect ourselves and my sister's son also tried.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "elements"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Blocks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: These are concrete blocks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I mean by elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Not furniture.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see anyone. They tried to protect us with these little rifles, but I did not see anyone there. I mean, the men did not have any weapons, only a few men who would stand guard had some weapons, but we did not have a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go back to the transcript. "Elements" are concrete blocks, so can we improve on the transcript. "Elements" are concrete blocks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honour. Is that a question, your Honour? If it is a statement by counsel, I do not understand where it is coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, is that a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No, my colleague told me that the reply of the witness was not included in the transcript, that is these "elements" meant concrete blocks, because perhaps the court reporter could not get that part of the testimony, that is why I asked the witness once again, so that we could correct the transcript, that is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, so it is not a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No. The people with these little rifles, how many were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I know that my son had a burned rifle, because we were in danger, he went to Visoko, I do not know if he had it there but I imagine that they leave their rifles behind when they go from the front-line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am asking about upper Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see anyone, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: One second, excuse me. I was not paying attention. What is the objection, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The objection is repetition, your Honour. We are back talking about rifles in the hands of Territorial Defence personnel, which we discussed on cross-examination earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The witness did not understand what I was saying and obviously not my learned colleague either. I just asked how many people were armed in Gornji Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: One second. I want to understand the point. Go ahead, repeat your question, Mr. Nobilo, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: My question was, how many people were armed in Gornji Ahmici, upper Ahmici when she came to the house where she sought shelter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see a single armed man then, only civilians, unarmed men went to see whether we could pass, whether they were holding the forest. I did not see anyone with a rifle there. It was women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So can we conclude that throughout this event, you did not see a single Muslim with a rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mentioned that the body of Osman was blown up by an explosive. Do you know who did that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eso Salkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know who did that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know a thing, I just saw his father crying and he was carrying something in a bag, I did not dare look. I was coming back from my sister's, where I spent the night because we were in danger, and I saw him and he was crying and he said, "look at what they are doing to us. What are we going to do? They killed my Eso last night".

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, when your son was extinguishing the fire in Pezer's house, when was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly, but it was before the conflict, quite a bit of time before the conflict, they burned the house of Muhamed Pezer in front of my house, between the bungalow and my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it at the time when there was that roadblock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not then. They were torching houses at night only.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that the local commune gave keys of weekend cottages for the refugees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How many refugees came to Ahmici, a lot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a lot, from Prijedor, Kozarac, Oborci, Karaula, from Karaula they mainly stayed in the neighbourhood in the weekend cottages near my house. Only my son was staying at Muhamed Spahic's house, the rest were refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said soldiers were hiding behind your balcony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Underneath my balcony, I was running away up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, this balcony, does it face the forest or the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It faces the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So it faces the cemetery. It is in the other direction, the opposite direction from the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is where the soldiers were, where my son was lying dead and I did not see anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, while they were hiding underneath your balcony, were shells, bullets hitting your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from a distance, from those two sides, not only bullets, shells also. Stronger explosions were heard and lesser explosions and that side of my house was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just one more question, I will not bother you any further. You said that your daughter did not tell you but somebody else about what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard her telling her friend, her girlfriend when we got out. I could not go into that line of conversation with her. I could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. (Pause).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She did tell me that they took off her gold jewellery.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, we have concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just briefly, Mr. President. The balcony that Mr. Nobilo was just asking you about that you said faces the cemetery, that balcony also faces towards the bungalow, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the bungalow is a bit further to the left-hand side, but they were shooting at us from Bahra and Hrazne, that area. Most of the shooting that morning came from that area, as far as my house is concerned. Whereas the people from Zume had a different story, they were hitting them from other places, from Radak, I do not know, but my house and what I went through, that is what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ms. Pjanic, just to clarify something, Mr. President, your son Muamer was murdered but your other son Mirza survived, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Fine, at present you have concluded your testimony, the Tribunal would like to thank you for clearing up these tragic incidents you experienced. We are going to adjourn now and we are going to resume at 2.45 pm this afternoon. (1.00 pm) (Adjourned until 2.45 pm) 20 21 22 23 24 25 (2.45 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The court is in session. Have the accused brought in. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Counsel for the Prosecution, I take it we are going to be hearing a protected witness? MS.. PATERSON: Yes, Mr. President. This witness has asked to have her face distorted and has asked to be referred to by a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. So this will be Witness N then, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you are expecting to hear from this witness before we bring her in, counsel? MS.. PATERSON: I did not, Mr. President. This witness is going to come a little bit out of order. She is not an Ahmici witness, she in fact lived in Vitez in April 1993, but for a variety of reasons she was not available to come here to The Hague earlier, so we have brought her on this occasion. She will be testifying basically about the events of 16th April a few days after that. As I said, she was living in Vitez at the time. She will describe briefly how her son was taken away by soldiers that morning to the veterinary station and from there he was taken out to dig trenches. Then she will discuss very briefly that a couple of days after that some three soldiers came to her house, basically looted the house, took money and gold from she and her family members and sexually assaulted her and raped her in her own home. She will discuss the fact that a night or two after that she unfortunately was sexually assaulted a second time in her home, by different perpetrators on that occasion. She will obviously describe the people involved, talk about the soldiers she saw in the area. She will talk about the fact that she was evacuated to some nearby homes, from which she saw a car full of men that she will identify as Vitezovi, pull up to the house, go into her house and essentially loot her house and steal her car. She will talk about some sightings of soldiers near houses that were burning and she will talk about how she was expelled from her home and a Croat family moved into her house after her family left. In addition, Mr. President, while we are very conscious of your desire to have us try and have the witnesses give their testimony in a narrative, because of the subject matter of this testimony this witness has specifically asked me that she not have to give this primarily as a narrative, that rather I put fairly specific questions to her and direct her testimony. In addition, she is not feeling well, too well physically. She does feel well enough to testify and would prefer to go ahead and get her testimony over today, but because of that I hope the court will be understanding that I will be somewhat more direct in my questioning than we have been doing with some of the other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. You have been rather direct so far, in fact, Ms. Paterson. But myself and fellow judges do agree, given the reasons given, that you direct the testimony along the appropriate lines. It is a matter of going to the essentials, really, whether it be the Prosecution or the Defence that is concerned. Our concern is that we all go to the essentials and if you bear that in mind, as you direct the testimony, I do not see that should be a problem at all. Maybe Mr. Harmon can answer this question, what does the rest of the week look like, because for the coming month we are going to have problems with the availability of the courtroom. We said Thursday morning we would not be able to sit because there was going to be a status conference relating to a different trial that would be lasting for a good while, that is before Trial Chamber II, and then Friday we will not be sitting. So we have this afternoon, all of tomorrow and Thursday afternoon; so Prosecutor, where do we stand in respect of witnesses? MR.. HARMON: Mr. President, this afternoon we have one witness and tomorrow we have two witnesses and that will conclude the witnesses who are available to us this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So given the time we have available, that is to say this afternoon, all of tomorrow and possibly Thursday afternoon, that should enable the witnesses to return home by Thursday evening at the latest, if not before that. MR.. HARMON: Yes, I would hope so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good. Then we have nothing to feel bad about, handing the courtroom over on Thursday morning to Trial Chamber II. Now Mr. Registrar, if you would please have Witness N brought in. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness N, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Now to begin with, this document will be shown to you. This has to do with verifying your identity. Do not say your name. Fine, thank you. Now please remain seated and read out the solemn declaration which the Registrar is going to put before you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I start?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Proceed, go ahead. WITNESS N (sworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now Witness N, you have agreed to come and testify before this Tribunal. You are a protected witness, special protective measures have been taken for you, so do feel safe, speak without any fear. The Prosecution will be putting some questions to you, I believe you have expressed the desire that questions be put to you by the Prosecution, with respect to the tragic incidents you lived through. Thereafter, as you were probably told, it is the Defence counsel who will be putting questions to you as well, and then the judges might be putting questions to you thereafter. If you do not feel well, please do not be shy, let us know, and we will interrupt as and when necessary. Ms. Paterson, please proceed. Examined by MS.. PATERSON

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Witness N, perhaps before we begin you might want to pull your chair up to the edge of the desk, you may be more comfortable and it will be easier for us to hear your answers. Witness N, in April 1993 were you living in the town of Vitez in Bosnia-Herzegovina with your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were the family members that lived with you at that time your two sons, your brother-in-law and your sister-in-law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did your husband also live with you at your home in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Why was your husband not present at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My husband was driving for the humanitarian aid vehicles from Croatia and so he was in Croatia at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you and members of your family Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, now I would like to direct your attention to 16th April 1993, early that morning. Did two soldiers come to your house on that morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the morning, between 5.00 and 5.30, I do not know exactly. They arrived in front of the house, they knocked and banged at the door. When I opened up, they were -- their faces were painted and they were looking for my son. My son was under age and I was surprised they were looking for him. I did not know where they were taking him. They took them to the camp -- they took him to the camp, as well as my neighbours. That is what I saw when I saw him off to the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the court what these soldiers looked like? I believe you said they had some paint on their faces. Can you describe what clothing they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recall if they were wearing any type of military clothing, or were they wearing civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was military clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said that they took your son away to the camp. Which camp are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the vet station down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was that your older son or your younger son that was taken away that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The older son.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you subsequently learn what happened to your son when he was detained at that camp at the veterinary station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken from the veterinary station to the school in Dubravica, and my son went to the cinema building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: While your son was detained at those different locations, was he also taken out to dig trenches at the front-lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, now Witness N, I would like to now direct your attention to a couple of days after 16th April 1993. Were you still living in your house in Vitez on that occasion, two or three days after 16th April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When my son was taken away, I was left alone in my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On one day some time after the 16th, did three men come to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, three men came to my house. They also knocked and banged. They broke down -- they broke the glass of the entrance door. When I opened up, the two of them went upstairs and one remained on the ground floor, where we were sitting. One of the two came and took me upstairs. He had a rifle. When he brought me into the room, he locked himself in the living room with me and the one who was downstairs, they were knocking on the door, they said, "do you want something?". I was not clear what he meant, do I want or not, because he threatened that he would break everything. This one said, "wait", and this one asked me whether I had any gold, any weapons, any money, and I said I did not have any weapons, any money, because my husband took the money to Croatia in order to buy some things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what these three men looked like? What kind of clothing were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wore civilian clothes. One of them only had camouflage trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. You said that one of the men took you upstairs. When he took you upstairs, did he sexually assault you at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: After the first man had done that to you, did the second man come into the room and also sexually assault you at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: While this was going on, while you were upstairs with the two men, was the third man downstairs with your son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He also asked weapons and money and gold from him, and my son told him the truth, that we did not have any money or gold or weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recall a statement that the man downstairs made to your son when he did take some jewellery or some of your possessions away from your son? Do you remember what he said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He said, "my mother has something in her purse", and said that it was some jewellery, it was not gold. He said, "is this gilded?". The boy did not know and he said yes, and then the soldier said, "we need this for the army", and he put it in his pocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The man that was downstairs, the man that took this jewellery, was he the one that was dressed partially in camouflage, or was he in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So could you describe what he was wearing then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a pair of trousers and a sweatshirt, some kind of civilian clothes, I was not looking at him very closely, because he remained downstairs and I was taken upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At some point in time, did the three men leave your house and do you know why they left when they did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When my boy dropped the contents of the bag, he said the ID card fell out, and so they all eventually left. MR.. HAYMAN: I apologise for interrupting the witness and counsel. I have spoken to my colleague, your Honour, and the answer that was translated, "he was not in civilian clothes" -- it has just gone off the screen, maybe it can be brought back down, I do not know -- Mr. Nobilo advises that what was said was, "he was in civilian clothes", this is the man downstairs. A moment later the witness described he was wearing trousers and a sweatshirt, he was wearing civilian clothes. I do not know how we do this, but there was an error in the translation and the transcript, I wanted to note it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman, these are translation problems by the interpreters. Mr. Registrar, could we fix that? Do we have a procedure?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, we do and we will set it right, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We do apologise. Please go on answering the counsel's questions, Witness N. MS.. PATERSON: Witness N, one more question concerning this day. There were three men who came to your house. Did you previously tell me that one of the men was in camouflage uniform, one was in civilian clothes and one was half in camouflage and half in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember that very well, it has been five or six years now. I cannot recall that. I only know that the small man was in civilian clothes. When they came up to me, I was already too afraid. I could have remembered it then, but I cannot remember it now any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, that is fine. As a result of these assaults that happened to you on that day, did you then become afraid to stay in your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would you tell the court what you decided to do because of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know. My brother-in-law left and we put a woman's dress and scarf on him, because all men were taken to the camp and he was hiding in my pantry. My neighbour was there and she told me -- he said, "pack up your bags for you and your child, we cannot wait here any longer, to have all the things that have been going on continue". I took the child's clothes and my own and put them in a bag and we were going to flee over to the neighbours. When I came to the road, I saw the houses on fire. Two soldiers noticed me and started running after me. They said, "where are you running? Fuck you". They had socks over their faces and I could not recognise them. They entered the house and looked around everywhere, went upstairs and one of them came over to me and he said, what was this. I said, "everything has been ransacked and everything has been broken". I told him, "you see what it is", "and what happened to you?", and I said, "nothing" because I did not dare talk. He asked me three times what happened and then I had to tell him what happened to me. One of them started to taunt me and the other one said, "fuck her, she is useless". Then they went out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. On that occasion when the two men came into the house, did one of those two men also sexually assault you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, neither of the two did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I want to stay on that day for just a couple more questions. You said you went out into the street planning to go to a neighbour's house and you said you saw some houses on fire, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the houses were on fire and those two men came from these houses, because I was going to go to the neighbours because I was afraid to stay in the house, so they noticed, I came halfway down the street, so they came running after me. They did not have their socks down their faces right away. When they closed in on me, they had these socks over their faces. So they came, the door was broken, the glass was shattered. They said, where was I running, fuck me. I opened the door and I said -- I was too afraid to say that I was looking for some kind of shelter in the neighbourhood. I said that I was going to the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you saw those houses burning, could you tell whether they were Muslim houses or whether they were Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim houses. MR.. NOBILO: Apology, there is another problem in the interpretation. There was a curse here which was interpreted as if they were cursing her directly, but what they said was a more general curse which was not directed directly at a lady, and it was not rendered correctly. It is not the most important thing, but in the context maybe it has more significance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I do not know, I have to look at the interpreting booths. So far we have not had any problems. Mr. Nobilo speaks the same language as the witness, I do not know what the interpreters think and what the counsel for the Prosecution makes of this. It is significant that we have precise rendition of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the easiest thing would simply be to put the question to the witness again and let her repeat it and see if we can get it correct. In addition, I have no problem at the end of my questioning to discuss any problems of this sort, but I request I be permitted to put my questions to the witness and then we deal with any challenges to the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, we can rephrase the question to the witness, but it is not all that great a way of proceeding, having the witness repeat, because you yourself in this procedure, counsel, you know pretty much what the counsel was going to say, so did you hear anything that struck you as different from what you expected from the witness? You are the only one really who can tell us. It is not a matter of being indiscreet, it is really the only way. You knew in advance, having spoken to the witness, what the witness's reply was going to be, so you were not surprised by that answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, unfortunately I do not speak the language of the witness. I also must rely on the interpretation, but the point is, she said that a derogatory comment was made to her. I do not honestly feel it is particularly significant what the exact words were. It was obvious it was meant to be derogatory and not a positive thing that was being said to her, but if I can tell from the way the witness is acting, I think she is prepared to answer the question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Okay, fine. We will put the question to the witness again, but still, Mr. Nobilo was not saying anything inappropriate, I think he is quite right with his point in wanting to set the record straight when the interpretation has not been perfect. So let us just hope that the incident is over and done with. Please, Ms. Paterson, if you would be so good as to put the question to the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Witness N, you probably heard the discussion we just had. Before when you were answering my question you said one of the men made a derogatory comment to you. Could you just please state again what this man said to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When he came to the door, I thought that there were neighbours underneath these socks, and I said -- he said, "why are you trying to run away?". Then he said through the door, "I beg your pardon" -- I was not saying this, they were saying it. They were cursing the mother of God to me through the door, and I said, "I am going to the basement". I do not know, I am perplexed, I am confused. I am trembling, I am shaking all over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. When you first saw these men near the burning houses, can you just explain where they were standing in relation to these burning houses. Were they standing close to the houses that were burning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were standing near the houses, near the houses, the houses that were burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not hear your answer when Mr. Nobilo interrupted before. Did you say that these were Muslim houses that were on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: These two soldiers that you saw near the burning house, can you describe what they were wearing? Were they wearing military clothing or were they wearing civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. You mentioned that you thought that perhaps these men were neighbours of yours. What exactly do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because they put socks over their faces so that I could not recognise them, that is what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you think they were trying to hide their identity from you by doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Later that same night, did some additional men, perhaps different men, perhaps the same, come to your house and again knock on your door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was night-time. They came and they knocked at the door courteously, and I went out. There were two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What happened when you went out and spoke with them on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That night, you said that two soldiers came to your door and knocked on the door. When they knocked on the door, did they say something to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they came and they had heard about the rape and they wanted to take me to another house. I went out, I do not know who it was, I went to the neighbourhood. Not one person, only there was a house next door, and I was there, I did not want to leave the house. I thought they would kill me again or something like that. They beseeched me to come out, because the next day others would come, so we all got out of the house, all of us who were there and I was watching through the window. There were soldiers with a car and it said, "Vitezovi" on the back. They went into the house, they went around the house, they took my car away then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me just ask you a couple more questions about that incident. You said that it was two soldiers that came to your door and they said they had heard you had been raped. Had you told anyone at that point in time what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not tell anyone because I had not left the house before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So do you have any idea how these men could know that you had been raped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They probably heard from one another, I do not know. I had not left the house before that, until that night, and then I did not go back to my home any more, I was hiding in one house and another house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: These two soldiers that came to your house that night, were they Croats or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Croats, because all the Muslims were detained, there were not any Muslims walking around, only civilians, women and children, were in the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Had you ever met those two soldiers before? Did you know them from the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No you did not know those soldiers, is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they came to evacuate us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When the two soldiers came and knocked on your door and said they had heard you had been raped, did you know either of those two soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. It was night-time and I was afraid, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. You said that they mentioned something to you that you should leave the house because it was not safe to stay there. Can you recall exactly what it was they said to you and why they said you should leave the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you remember if they said that you should leave the house that night because more soldiers would come the next day and you would be killed by those soldiers; is that what they said to you that night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spoke about that, they were coming as I had already left the house, I saw it from my neighbour's place. The next day they came. I was terrified as I saw all of that. I saw their car, and "Vitezovi" was written on the back of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you saw this car --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a blue "101".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you saw this car that had the Vitezovi sticker on it, this was the next day after these men had come and knocked on your door, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The very next day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many men got out of this car that had the Vitezovi sticker on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not count them, some of them went into the house, others went around the house, I was not watching them very carefully, I was frightened and I feared for my own safety. It was terrible watching them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, and did you notice what these soldiers were wearing, whether they were wearing military clothing or civilian clothing and what colour it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in those black clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you know what the term or the phrase "Vitezovi" meant? Had you ever seen that before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the fact that there was an organisation in Vitez that was operating and going by the name of Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war, I knew about the HOS, they were called. What they turned into, I do not know; Vitezovi, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. After this incident when the men came in this car and took things from your house, were you ever able to return to your house after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because a soldier came after they had taken the car away. He said, "you can go back to your home now". I had animals, I had a cow and chickens and a neighbour would go there and feed them, she did that, I did not dare go, and when they took the car away, then this neighbour said we could go back. Those who would pass by would not be coming back any more, he said, "you can go back freely". I was not the only one who returned, all my women neighbours returned to their homes then. So we were there for some time, but I saw that there could not be any safety there, so I disappeared from Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was your house burned or significantly destroyed in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not burned at all. It was not burned at all. It remained intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know if anyone is currently living in your house in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At some point in time, were you informed that a Croat family had moved into your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a Croat family had moved in, but this changes, different people move in, yes, it was a Croat family that was moved in, yes. Not only my house but of all my neighbours, all my neighbours left, so it is only normal that Croats moved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you say all your neighbours moved out, do you mean all your Muslim neighbours moved out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that some of the Muslim houses were burned, because you previously described seeing a house on fire, and some of them were left intact, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were burned down, some were burned down while I was there in the neighbourhood and then as I was running away, two were on fire -- five or six, there were a lot of them that were torched, Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recall the approximate date that you finally left Vitez and moved elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. It was shocking and I was very frightened. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was it some time in the summer of 1993 that you left Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was the same year, the same year. Perhaps I had not even spent a month there -- no, not a month, no, then I left.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness N. Mr. President, I have no further questions of this witness at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is an unusual request, but could we the Defence counsel have a moment to confer with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In the presence of the witness that you would have a discussion? It is about this testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It is, and off the record. It is an unusual request, I can explain it to the court outside of the presence of the witness. I think we can walk over there and talk to them for 30 seconds and that would be my request.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: We have no objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. How do you want to proceed? Should we ask Witness N to remain here, would you prefer a closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We can walk over, if the court will pardon us from walking through the well, and simply speak to them privately for a moment and then we will know how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The well is not insurmountable. You just work it out, but do tell us how much time you want to have available. It is not all that pleasant for the witness for the judges to remain sitting here. How much time are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would think a couple of minutes, and I know it is not as respectful as I would like to be, to be keeping the court waiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That is not the issue. The judges will not remain seated here in the courtroom. We are going to have a short break, the Registrar will inform us when you are ready to resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (3.45 pm) (A short break) (3.55 pm) (In the absence of the witness)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The court is back in session, please be seated. Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, before Mr. Hayman begins, we would like to request that this be done in a closed session, private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I was simply going to say, your Honour, that we did have a chance to speak to the prosecutors during the break, I thank you for that. We were not able to reach any agreement that might shorten this witness's testimony and we are prepared to proceed with cross-examination. I thank the court for the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well then, if I have grasped all this, the judges have to note that there is non-agreement on a subject the judges know absolutely nothing about. So there is a disagreement. I take it the incident is over and done with and that the witness may be shown back in, Witness N. The matter is over with, is it, Ms. Paterson?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, if you can just give me one moment to consult with my colleagues? (Pause).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ms. Paterson?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Mr. Hayman is correct in that there was not a meeting of the minds between Mr. Hayman and the prosecutors. However, we feel it should go on the record that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a second here. What would you like to have on the record?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: That the issue that Mr. Hayman raised with us is that he raised a Rule 68 ethical violation, claiming that the testimony of this witness was, according to him, significantly different --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Hold it, Ms. Paterson. I would just like to hold it here for a second. The judges are willing to go along with anything you would like. Mr. Hayman just asked us for a break, it is rather unusual that the judges have to leave the courtroom when a matter is raised. I am willing to have everything go on record, but on behalf of fellow judges, I would ask that we be informed as to what it is about. I am not a public notary, I am not a scribe, I would like to know what is the issue here. We gave you a recess and we learned in the course thereof that the witness was not feeling well; we asked the Registrar to see the witness out, but it is a matter of dignity here as well for the judges, it is not just of us taking stock. Mr. Hayman, can you tell us very briefly what the issue was, where the issue lies, why the witness is no longer here, and then we will put whatever in the transcript. I do not think it would be appropriate that you decide what goes in the transcript in respect of a matter we know absolutely nothing about. What was this whole incident about, please, Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will address that, your Honour. I would note that I think it is helpful at certain unique times for the parties to be able to have confidential discussions and to try and reach agreements to further the proceedings. That is what I thought I had in the corridor with the Prosecutor. It now appears they are intent on disclosing those discussions to the court, in violation of the confidence that I thought we had, but in any event, I would like to simply state that we suggested that the witness discontinue her testimony and that the parties stipulate to the court and recommend to the court that she be withdrawn as a witness. The parties were unable to agree on that and hence we believe we should proceed. As to why we suggested that, I think it was a matter that the Defence should be entitled to raise in confidence as a confidential off-the-record matter with the Prosecutor. On the other hand, if the Prosecutor is determined to go into it, then I would like to speak to it at that time to share our views. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Hayman. Thank you very much indeed. That is what I wanted. I did not want to know about the exact contents of your conversations with the Prosecutor. The only thing I wanted to achieve is not to be here with my colleagues as just spectators to a table tennis game and just there to register transcripts. This is not what judges are about, so Ms. Paterson, you confirm what Mr. Hayman has just said? I am not asking you why you did not agree together, that is your business, but you confirm what Mr. Hayman has just said so we can carry on, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, in substance, I agree with what Mr. Hayman said. However, in the course of that conversation he raised what he felt was a Rule 68 violation and he felt we had not disclosed something we were obligated to disclose. We take that as a very serious matter and we felt that because of the nature of what was being raised that the court should be made aware of it and that it should go on the record, so that it is clear that what Mr. Hayman is claiming happened did, in fact, not happen. We are prepared to address the issue, if need be we will submit the witness's statement for review. We just feel that it is a significant enough issue that the court should be made aware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. We are not going to go into the actual contents of the dispute, but now we know what has to be put on record, we note that as far as Mr. Hayman is concerned, he thinks that there is a violation as to the Rule 68 provision. This will be submitted, we shall appreciate as judges when the time comes to assess the scope of the testimony as such. The matter is settled. Mr. Hayman, do you have anything to add? You are not happy with what Judge Jorda has just said?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Only to say, I did not make any claim of a Rule 68 violation to the court and I think for the Prosecutor to now put the statement of the witness in front of the court, I think that is wrong, it is an out of court hearsay statement. If they are going to do that then in our cross-examination we are going to have to go through all the material elements of that statement and it is going to greatly prolong the cross. I did not make an allegation to the court that they violated Rule 68. I had a private discussion with them and I sought their views. They shared their views with me and now they are trying to use this incident to put the witness's written statement in front of the court and I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. I can only repeat what I have just said, the matter is settled. You shall proceed to the cross-examination as I originally intended. You insisted on being able to have a conversation with the Prosecutor, but the matter is now settled. We can have the witness in and the cross-examination will be what it is and we shall make sure it remains within the scope of the examination-in-chief. I hope that the witness is able to put up with cross-examination. You were finished, were you not, Ms. Paterson?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we had finished our questioning of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Is Mr. Nobilo going to lead the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, very, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We know how courteous you are when you cross-examine witnesses who are victims of this tragedy and we trust you once again. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness N, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you feel better? Are you feeling somewhat better than before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am upset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness N, after the statements we have made to the Prosecutor, you are now going to have questions put by Mr. Nobilo, who is the Defence counsel of General Blaskic. Remember at all times that you are under protection and the protection of the judges, so we trust that Mr. Nobilo is going to proceed to the cross-examination of the points that are relevant for the Defence of his client, General Blaskic. Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Witness N, as the President said, I am going to put a few questions to you. I know that you are upset, it is going to be very, very brief so that we do not keep you very long. I am interested in the following. Before the Vitezovi came to your house and before they stole your car, the two soldiers that came and took you to the other house, did you take this as an act of protection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were they kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, this unfortunate incident that happened to you, during your stay in Vitez, did you report this to the police or to the military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not report it to anyone, I did not dare go out of my house. I did not go out at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, after the Vitezovi left and until you left Vitez, did anybody threaten you or come to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ms. Paterson, do you have any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So Witness N, this is over, I hope you will get better and you will make your way home. Try and forget, if you can. The Tribunal thanks you very much. Make sure that all the protective measures are taken to allow Witness N to go out of the courtroom. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, are you the one introducing the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we do not have any additional witnesses for today. We have concluded with the available witnesses for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, so we shall resume again tomorrow morning at 10.00, and we are going to hear the last two witnesses for the week, is that right, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The hearing is adjourned. We will resume tomorrow morning at 10.00. (4.15 pm)

procedural_notes.text: (Hearing adjourned until 10.00 am the following day)
